meta.name: CDU First-Year Student Support knowledge base
meta.primary_source: New Student Welcome Centre FAQ, Version 2 (28/02/2023), provided by the CDU Senior Student Success Adviser
meta.notes: Answers rewritten from staff-facing wording into student-facing chat wording without changing meaning. Internal staff-only escalation notes removed. Entries with review_flag need a staff check before go-live. Entries with approved=false are team-written placeholders for unit-level questions, pending staff approval.

faqs.question: Where can I find everything I need as a new student?
alternatives: I'm a new student, where do I start?
first year student getting started guide
what should I do first when I start at CDU
faqs.answer:
The best place to start is the **New to CDU** page. It walks you through activating your account, enrolling, setting up IT and getting your timetable.

If you'd like one-on-one help with account activation, enrolment, study plans or timetables, visit the support staff in the **Library Foyer** (ITMS, Student Central and Library staff are based there).

faqs.question: How do I activate my student account?
alternatives: how to set up my student login
I can't log in, my account isn't activated
where do I activate my student email
how do I get my username and password
faqs.answer:
Go to **activation.cdu.edu.au** and step through the prompts. The New to CDU page also has the full set of steps.

If you get stuck, the support staff in the Library Foyer can help you one-on-one.

faqs.question: What do I need to do to set up IT access?
alternatives: how do I set up multi-factor authentication
authenticator app setup for my student account
faqs.answer: After activating your account, set up **Microsoft Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)**. This keeps your account secure, and you'll need it to sign in to CDU systems and the CDU app.

faqs.question: How do I get a student card?
alternatives: where do I get my student ID card
how to get my ID card
faqs.answer:
- **Casuarina:** CDU Student Central or the IT staff in the Library can print your student card, or you can go to Student Central in Orange 1.
- **Danala:** go to the Student Central desk.

Bring **photo ID** (such as your passport). It's required for your first card.

faqs.question: I need help with enrolling
alternatives: how do I enrol in my units
how do I pick my units
can't enrol in a unit prerequisite not completed
how do I enrol in an intensive unit
faqs.answer:
Start with the **Guide to Enrolling** (Current Students > Student admin > Guide to enrolling).

Some special enrolments can only be done manually using an **eForm**:
- a prerequisite hasn't been completed
- overload (not available to first-semester students)
- intensive units
- other provisional enrolments approved by your Faculty or the Higher Education Enrolment team

For one-on-one help, visit the support staff in the Library Foyer.

faqs.question: How do I access my study plan?
alternatives: what units do I need to do this semester
faqs.answer:
Search **study plan** on AskCDU, CDU's FAQ site, for step-by-step help.

Make sure you look at the study plan for the **semester you're starting in** (for example, the Semester 2 plan if you start mid-year).

faqs.question: Where can I find my timetable?
alternatives: how do I see my class schedule
where do I check my class times
faqs.answer:
- **Higher Education students:** your timetable is in the **New Student Portal**, which should show all your classes.
- **TAFE students:** your lecturer gives you your timetable. After you apply, they'll contact you to discuss your units and timetable.

faqs.question: How do I apply for a USI?
alternatives: what is a unique student identifier
where do I enter my USI
faqs.answer:
Getting a **Unique Student Identifier (USI)** is quick, easy and free.

1. Have a valid form of ID ready.
2. Create your USI on the USI Registry System.
3. Enter your USI in **My Student Info**, under Enrolment Steps.

Your USI is needed for CDU's government reporting, and for international students it also matters for visa compliance.

faqs.question: As an international student, what do I need to update in My Student Info?
alternatives: which address do I put in my student info
do I need a semester address
faqs.answer:
Please check your details in **My Student Info**. It's vital for CDU's government reporting and your visa compliance.

- **Contact Details:** enter your **Australian address**.
- **Home Address and Emergency Contact:** enter your **home-country address** and an emergency contact number.
- The Semester Address is **not** compulsory.

Also make sure your **USI** is entered under Enrolment Steps.

faqs.question: How do I get access to Wi-Fi?
alternatives: how to connect my laptop to the internet at uni
faqs.answer:
You can use Wi-Fi once your **student account is activated**. **eduroam** is the preferred network. It works on all CDU campuses and at many universities in Australia and around the world.

1. Select the **eduroam** network.
2. Username: **s123456@students.cdu.edu.au** (your student number)
3. Password: your current CDU password

On some Android phones you may also need to set the domain to **cdu.edu.au**.

faqs.question: Can I meet with someone to help me with IT questions?
alternatives: who do I contact for IT problems
my laptop won't connect who can help
faqs.answer:
- **Casuarina:** go to the **ITMS kiosk** in the Library.
- **Danala:** ask at Student Central.
- **Phone:** 08 8946 6600

faqs.question: How do I get help navigating the Library resources?
alternatives: how do I use the library
faqs.answer: Visit the **CDU Library website** and its **New Student Guide to the Library**. Library staff can also help you in person.

faqs.question: How do I print on campus?
alternatives: how much printing do I get
where can I print my assignment
faqs.answer:
Students get a **$10 printing quota per semester**.

At Casuarina and Danala you can print from your own computer using **Web Print** in **My-Print**.

faqs.question: How do I get help with assignment writing and referencing?
alternatives: someone to check my draft assignment
faqs.answer:
- **On Casuarina campus:** the Library runs **Write Right** sessions (bring your draft and check you're on the right track) and **referencing workshops**. Check LibCal for current dates.
- **Online students:** use CDU's **Language and Learning Support** service.
- **Any time:** online recorded resources are available.

You can also book individual appointments with **Language & Learning Advisors**.
faqs.review_flag: The source notes Write Right may not run every semester. Check current LibCal listings.

faqs.question: How can I improve my English?
faqs.answer:
- **Casuarina:** join the **Chance2Chat** workshop.
- **Palmerston:** **English Language for the Workplace** sessions (see LibCal).
- **Online:** **English Club** workshops on pronunciation, grammar, reading and vocabulary.

You can also book one-on-one appointments with a **Language & Learning Advisor**.
faqs.review_flag: Workshop schedules change each semester. Confirm these are still running.

faqs.question: How can I improve my study skills?
faqs.answer:
CDU has **online Study skills resources** on its website.

Other options:
- **Peer Advisors** give informal study help from fellow students.
- **Online Tutoring** (via Learnline) offers 24/7 subject-specific help by text or phone.
- **Language & Learning Advisors** offer individual appointments.

faqs.question: How do I borrow or request library resources?
alternatives: library doesn't have the book I need
faqs.answer:
You can **reserve, borrow and return** resources through the Library (see the Borrowing page).

If something isn't available, use the **purchase request form** to recommend a resource. To suggest a journal subscription or database, contact a Librarian.

faqs.question: How do I book a study room in the Casuarina Library?
alternatives: reserve a room in the library
faqs.answer: You can book a study room for **up to 2 hours a day** through **LibCal** (Space Availability, Casuarina).

faqs.question: Can I use the libraries on other campuses?
alternatives: can I go to the Palmerston library
faqs.answer: Yes. You can access all CDU libraries with your **student card**. If your card doesn't work, ask the library staff or the IT team.

faqs.question: Is there a wayfinding app for CDU?
alternatives: how do I find my way around campus
faqs.answer: Yes. Download the **CDU** app from your app store. You'll sign in with your CDU student account, so **activate your account and set up MFA** first.

faqs.question: How do I read room and building locations?
faqs.answer:
At Casuarina, rooms follow this format:
**[Precinct colour + building number] . [level] . [room number]**

For example, **Blue 5.1.24** is building Blue 5, level 1, room 24. Other CDU campuses use a very similar format.

At **Danala**, there's a map in each foyer next to the lifts.

faqs.question: Where can I download a campus map?
faqs.answer: Downloadable maps are available for **Casuarina**, **Palmerston** and **Alice Springs** campuses on the CDU website. You can also use the **CDU app** for wayfinding.

faqs.question: Where can I park on campus?
faqs.answer: See CDU's **Parking facilities** page for where to park and any permit details.

faqs.question: Are there campus tours on open days or orientation days?
alternatives: can someone show me around campus
faqs.answer: Yes. Campus tours run from the **face-to-face Welcome Centres** during orientation.

faqs.question: How can I get help with accommodation?
alternatives: find a place to rent in Darwin
faqs.answer:
Start at CDU **Accommodation Services**. Options include:
- **CDU Village:** join the waitlist for a long-term room.
- **Study Stays:** CDU's off-campus listings (usually shared houses or granny flats). Only CDU students can view it.
- **Unilodge** near Casuarina Shopping Centre (shared accommodation).
- **Homestay:** Global Experience or Australian Homestay Network, for short stays of up to about 8 weeks.
- General sites: **Flatmates.com.au**, **realestate.com.au**, **Gumtree** and the Facebook group *Buy Swap Sell Wanted Darwin*.
- **Airbnb** works as a temporary option but is expensive, especially in the dry season (May to October).

faqs.question: I've arrived and don't have anywhere to stay tonight
alternatives: I have nowhere to sleep tonight
need somewhere to stay right now
faqs.answer:
**CLV** has rooms for students who need **emergency accommodation**. Stays are limited so CLV can help as many students as possible, and availability depends on demand.

Call **+61 8 7928 5050**.

If you're unsafe right now, call **000**.
faqs.review_flag: The source uses both 'CLV' and 'CVL'. Confirm the provider's full name and phone number with staff.

faqs.question: How can I meet new friends on campus?
alternatives: I feel lonely and want to meet people
faqs.answer:
- **Student Portal:** log in to find **Student Groups** and upcoming **Events**.
- **Buddy Program** (international students): meet a buddy before classes start. Contact CDU Global at international@cdu.edu.au. *It doesn't run every semester, so check with CDU Global.*
- **Student lounges:** Casuarina (Red 1, Level 3) and Danala (Levels 3 and 4).
- **Student Leaders** organise events and are a first point of contact for peer support.
faqs.review_flag: Staff note: CDU Global confirmed the Buddy Program wasn't running in one semester. Check its current status.

faqs.question: Is there a student lounge on campus?
alternatives: where can I heat my lunch
faqs.answer:
- **Casuarina:** Student Lounge at the top of **Red 1, Level 3**, open 8:30am to 4:00pm for CDU students. It has a fridge, microwaves, a table-tennis table, lounges, bean bags and tables.
- **Danala:** student lounges on **Level 3 and Level 4**, each with a kitchen area.

faqs.question: How can I fit into the Darwin community?
faqs.answer:
- Look for local events on Facebook and the **City of Darwin** website.
- **Volunteer:** try the Careers Centre's **VALUE Program** (Volunteer and Learn) or **Volunteering NT**.
- Join local events and activities.

faqs.question: How can I build professional connections?
faqs.answer:
The **Careers Centre** offers workshops, drop-in sessions and career consultations (by appointment). You can reach it through the Student Portal.

Current programs:
- **AWESOME Program:** Australian work experience
- **Mentor Program:** insight from industry
- **VALUE Program:** volunteer and learn

faqs.question: What are CDU's social media accounts?
faqs.answer:
Find these on Facebook, Instagram, X (Twitter) and TikTok:
- Charles Darwin University
- CDU Careers Centre
- CDU Student Life
- CDU Library

faqs.question: Is there a CDU bus between Danala and Casuarina?
faqs.answer: Yes. The CDU bus runs on a **fixed timetable**. Search **Bus service** on the CDU website for the latest times.

faqs.question: What public transport options are there in Darwin?
alternatives: how do I get to campus by bus
faqs.answer:
Buses run between **Darwin City, Casuarina and Palmerston**. CDU students get a **concession fare seven days a week**. Show your **student ID card** to the driver.

Services can change at short notice, and timetables are updated on Monday mornings. For updates, see the **CDC NT** Facebook page, call **08 8944 2444**, or use the bus tracker app.
faqs.review_flag: The source says buses were free 'for some time'. That wording is left out because it's likely out of date. Check current fares.

faqs.question: How do I pay for buses in Darwin?
alternatives: where to buy a bus card
faqs.answer: You can buy a ticket or a **Tap and Ride** card. A **concession** Tap and Ride card is available from the bus interchanges in **Darwin and Casuarina**. Bring your **student ID card** to get it.

faqs.question: I have a driver's licence. Can I drive in the Northern Territory?
alternatives: can I drive with my foreign license
faqs.answer:
You can drive in the NT on your overseas licence for a **limited time**.

- If your licence isn't in English, you need an **International Driving Permit**, or an official English translation from an authorised translator in the NT. Carry it with your licence whenever you drive.
- If you stay in the NT **for more than 3 months**, you must transfer to an **NT driver licence**.

links.label: NT licence rules for new residents

faqs.question: How do I get help finding a job?
alternatives: how do I get a job in Darwin
faqs.answer:
The **Careers Centre** can help:
- Log in to the Careers Centre through the **CDU Portal** and click the green **How do I get a job?** tile.
- Attend the **How to find work in Australia?** workshop. Register under *Events and appointments*.

faqs.question: Can someone check my resume?
faqs.answer: Yes. Log in to the Careers Centre through the **CDU Portal** and use the **CV Review** tool under *Job application tools*. After that, book an appointment with a **Careers Consultant** under *Events and appointments*.

faqs.question: How do I get my overseas qualification assessed?
faqs.answer: Contact the **Skills Recognition Centre**.

faqs.question: I have a question about my visa and working hours. How do I get help?
alternatives: how many hours can I work on a student visa
faqs.answer:
Start with CDU's **Student visa** page.

For more detailed matters, use the **Compliance and enrolment** page for international students. This covers leave of absence, CoE extensions, reduced study load, OSHC, international scholarships and compliance issues.

For anything about your own visa, contact **CDU Global** at international@cdu.edu.au.

faqs.question: I'm an international student. How do I get a bank account and phone?
alternatives: open a bank account in Australia
just arrived in Darwin what do I do
faqs.answer: Everything for newly arrived international students, including banking and phones, is on CDU's **Upon arrival** page.

faqs.question: I accepted my offer but my status still says unconfirmed and I can't enrol
faqs.answer:
This often resolves itself:
- **Onshore:** allow about **48 hours** after accepting.
- **Offshore:** it can take about **5 working days** for your payment to arrive, which then changes your status to accepted.

If it's past that time, or you have any other question about international enrolment, email **CDU Global** at international@cdu.edu.au.

faqs.question: Can I change to a different course and keep my Global Merit Scholarship?
alternatives: will I lose my scholarship if I change course
faqs.answer:
Yes, as long as your **new course is also eligible** for the Global Merit Scholarship (GMS).

- **Commencing students:** email international@cdu.edu.au to request the change.
- **Continuing students:** complete the **Course Transfer eForm**.
faqs.review_flag: Based on the 2024-2025 GMS terms and conditions. Check against the current T&Cs.

faqs.question: When do I need to pay my fees to keep my Global Merit Scholarship?
faqs.answer: Pay your fees by **close of business on the Census Date** of the semester you're enrolled in. If you have trouble paying, contact **Fees** straight away (fees@cdu.edu.au).
faqs.review_flag: Based on the 2024-2025 GMS terms and conditions. Check against the current T&Cs.

faqs.question: Can I hold more than one scholarship?
alternatives: Study NT scholarship and GMS together
faqs.answer: Generally you can hold only **one** scholarship. The exception is the **Study NT Scholarship**, which you can hold at the same time.
faqs.review_flag: Based on the 2024-2025 GMS terms and conditions. Check against the current T&Cs.

faqs.question: How many units do I need to enrol in to keep my Global Merit Scholarship?
alternatives: how many credit points per semester
faqs.answer:
Enrol in at least **80 credit points per year** (in line with student visa conditions), usually **40CP each in Semesters 1 and 2**, unless you have an approved **Reduced Study Load**.

If you can't take a full load (for example, because of a Learning Management Plan restriction), request a Reduced Study Load **before the deadline** and get approval from CDU Global.
faqs.review_flag: Based on the 2024-2025 GMS terms and conditions. Check against the current T&Cs.

faqs.question: If I fail a unit, do I lose my scholarship?
faqs.answer:
Not for a first fail. To keep the GMS you need to maintain **satisfactory academic progress**, or have a **Learning Management Plan** in place and seen by CDU Global.

- After a first fail, plan how to repeat the unit or find another pathway, especially if it's a core unit.
- Repeated fails can lead to an Under Review or Under Progression notice. If you're contacted by the Progression team, **respond and follow their guidance**.
- You may lose eligibility if you don't show improvement or don't tell CDU Global your plans.
faqs.review_flag: Based on the 2024-2025 GMS terms and conditions. Check against the current T&Cs.

faqs.question: What happens if I need to extend my CoE?
alternatives: need more time to finish my course visa
faqs.answer: Complete the **CoE extension request** on the CDU website and attach any supporting documents. CDU Global starts processing requests **after grades are released** for the semester. An outcome usually takes about **10 business days (2 weeks)** from grade release. Your GMS eligibility will be noted in the outcome.

faqs.question: Who do I contact about fees?
faqs.answer: Email **fees@cdu.edu.au**. Fees staff can look at your situation. This assistant can't see your account.

faqs.question: How do I make a complaint?
faqs.answer: Email **complaints@cdu.edu.au**. For independent advice on appeals, complaints or university policy, you can also contact **Student Advocacy**.

faqs.question: I'm a new international student and want to change my course or program
faqs.answer:
Email **international@cdu.edu.au** as soon as possible.
- Before classes start: use **Course Change** in the subject line and explain your reasons.
- Commencing students changing program: use **Change of Program** in the subject line.

Continuing students use the **Course Transfer eForm**.

faqs.question: Where can I get food at Danala?
faqs.answer: Danala has **food vending machines**, one at the entrance of Foyer 1. There's also a **café and a Woolworths** across the road at the front.

faqs.question: Where are the bathrooms at Danala?
faqs.answer: Bathrooms are **beside the lifts in each foyer**. They're also shown on the floor map on each level.

faqs.question: I'm feeling stressed or overwhelmed. Who can I talk to?
faqs.answer:
You don't have to handle this alone. **CDU Counselling** offers **free, confidential** support for personal, family, mental health or general wellbeing concerns.

- Email: **counselling@cdu.edu.au**
- Phone: **+61 8 8946 6288**
- In person: Blue 5, Casuarina

If you're in danger or need urgent help, call **000**, or **Lifeline 13 11 14** (24/7).

faqs.question: How do I contact campus security?
alternatives: walk me to my car at night
faqs.answer:
**CDU Security** provides **24/7** campus safety services.
- Phone: **+61 8 8946 6666**
- Office: Orange 2, Level 1, opposite Student Central
- Download the free **SafeZone** app to contact Security and Safety directly.

In an emergency, call **000**.

faqs.question: I have a disability or health condition. Can I get study adjustments?
faqs.answer:
Yes. **Access and Inclusion** supports students with disabilities or health conditions by arranging **reasonable adjustments**.
- Email: **inclusion@cdu.edu.au**
- Register through the Access and Inclusion page.

faqs.question: Who can give me independent advice about an appeal or unfair treatment?
faqs.answer: **Student Advocacy** gives independent support for academic appeals, complaints, fair treatment and understanding university policy. Submit an enquiry through the Student Advocacy page.

faqs.question: Is there support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students?
faqs.answer:
**First Nations Student Support** offers tailored support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students, including tutoring and cultural services.
- Email: **fnssreception@cdu.edu.au**
- Phone: **+61 8 8946 6479**

faqs.question: Where can international students get general support?
alternatives: I'm an international student and need help
who helps international students with wellbeing
faqs.answer:
**International Student Support (ISS)** helps with wellbeing, visa and academic support, and can point you to the right service.
- Email: **iss@cdu.edu.au**

For visa-related changes, contact **CDU Global** (international@cdu.edu.au).

faqs.question: Which student support service should I contact?
alternatives: who do I ask for help
where do I go for help
faqs.answer:
- **Student Central:** admin such as unit changes, RPL and enrolments
- **CDU Global:** visa-related changes for international students
- **International Student Support (iss@cdu.edu.au):** friendly help with any problem
- **Counselling:** emotional and mental health support
- **Language & Learning Advisors:** English and study support appointments
- **Peer Advisors:** informal study help from fellow students
- **Online Tutoring (via Learnline):** 24/7 subject help
- **Careers Centre:** jobs, resumes, internships, volunteering
- **Student Advocacy:** fair treatment, appeals, conflict resolution
- **Access and Inclusion:** adjustments for disability or health conditions

faqs.question: How do I contact Student Central?
faqs.answer:
**Student Central** handles admin such as enrolments, unit changes and RPL (credit transfer).
- Phone: **1800 061 963**
- Email: **student.central@cdu.edu.au**
- In person: Student Central in Orange 1 (Casuarina), or the support staff in the **Library Foyer**

faqs.question: How do I join my online class?
alternatives: where is the link for my online tutorial
faqs.answer:
Links to online classes are usually in your unit's **Learnline** site. Check the unit announcements and the weekly or Getting Started area.

If you can't find the link, contact your **unit coordinator or lecturer**. Their details are in the unit's Learnline site.
faqs.review_flag: Team-written placeholder for a unit-level question. Needs Student Success staff approval.

faqs.question: Where can I find recorded lectures?
alternatives: missed a lecture where is the recording
faqs.answer:
Recordings are usually posted in your unit's **Learnline** site. Each unit can organise them differently, so check the unit's menu and announcements.

If a recording is missing, ask your **unit coordinator or lecturer**.
faqs.review_flag: Team-written placeholder for a unit-level question. Needs Student Success staff approval.

faqs.question: When is my assessment due?
alternatives: where do I submit my assignment
faqs.answer:
Due dates and submission instructions are in your **unit outline** and in the **Assessment** area of your unit's **Learnline** site.

If you're unsure or need an extension, contact your **unit coordinator** before the due date.
faqs.review_flag: Team-written placeholder for a unit-level question. Needs Student Success staff approval.

faqs.question: Where do I find my unit materials?
alternatives: which folder are the readings in
can't find my unit on Learnline
faqs.answer:
Unit materials (slides, readings, weekly content) are in your unit's **Learnline** site. Lecturers organise folders differently, so start with the unit's Getting Started or Weekly Content area.

If a unit isn't showing in Learnline, check you're **enrolled** in it. Student Central can help with that.
